The posterior mixture of the candidates' conditional expectations

Source: R/cellgloc_categorical.R
dot-gloc_impute_mix.Rd

Under per-level detection (imputeCellGLoc(categorical = "em"), soft corner, since 7.5.1) a missing continuous cell of a row that also misses a categorical cell is imputed by \(\sum_k r_k E[x_{mis} | \textrm{cells clean under } k, u_k]\): .gloc_impute on the row's candidate rows, each at its own design row with its own cell weights, mixed by the candidates' posterior probabilities. That is the exact posterior mean of the missing cell.

.gloc_impute_mix(
  Xi,
  X,
  M,
  B,
  Sigma,
  cw,
  design,
  levels,
  w_min = 0.5,
  band = .gloc_peer_band
)

Arguments

Xi

the imputation so far, from .gloc_impute at the expected design rows; its non-mixture rows are the result's.

X, M

the continuous data and its missing mask.

B, Sigma

the fit's coefficients and scatter.

cw

the fit's cat_weights.

design

one-sided formula, the fit's.

levels

named list of levels, from .gloc_cat_prepare.

w_min, band

the peer rule.

Value

Xi with those cells replaced.

Details

Until 7.5.0 such a cell was imputed once, at the row's expected design row \(\bar u_i\). That was exact only because every level shared one weight row and hence one set of clean peers, so the conditional expectation was linear in the design row and the mixture could be taken inside it. Per-level detection breaks that: conditioning at \(\bar u_i\) on the mixture weights would condition on a cell with a weight that no candidate gave it, leaving detection and imputation inconsistent (Ruling R74).

Only the missing cells of the rows in cw are replaced, and only where the row has one; every other cell of Xi is returned untouched, bit for bit. A row above the combination cap is not in cw and keeps the 7.5.0 imputation. imputeCellGLoc and .gloc_draw_mi(noise = FALSE) both come through here, which is what makes the second reproduce the first exactly.
